page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. The system features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz across 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs. It includes 384.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources also include 3,600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and 20 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, with zero discrete GPUs present.

Benchmark measurements highlight strong parallel processing and encryption capabilities alongside notable single-threaded constraints. Due to the older first-generation EPYC architecture and modest clock speeds, single-core metrics fall into the bottom 10%, shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 590.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 725.0. Conversely, broad core density yields solid multi-core execution, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,199.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 47,316.06. Hardware-assisted cryptography provides strong performance, reaching 77,626.79 on the PassMark CPU encryption test.

Data handling and memory bandwidth tests show consistent multi-threaded throughput. Cached read operations achieve 3,712.61 GB/sec, while uncached 256MB memory reads register at 181.6 GB/sec and writes reach 89.72 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput measures 55.68 million operations per second, complemented by PassMark database operations at 15,575.26. For machine learning inference, prompt processing reaches 997.24 tokens/sec on a 135M model and 50.78 tokens/sec on a 7B model, though large-model (70B) prompt processing drops to 5.37 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m5ad.24xlarge delivers dense aggregate compute, generous memory capacity, and substantial fast NVMe scratch storage. Tradeoffs center on low per-core performance and the lack of newer vector instruction sets like AVX-512. The instance is suited for multi-threaded distributed workloads, batch processing, data transformation, caching tiers, and relational databases that benefit from high core counts and low-latency local NVMe storage rather than maximum single-thread performance.
description: Amazon Web Services m5ad.24xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual machine configured with an AMD EPYC 7571 processor delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores at 2.2 GHz. It is paired with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 3,600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Without discrete GPUs, computing workloads rely entirely on the CPU array. While single-thread benchmarks place in lower percentiles due to modest clock speeds, the 96 vCPUs achieve competitive aggregate throughput in multi-core metrics, data compression, and hardware-accelerated encryption. Memory bandwidth and database operational tests demonstrate solid handling of high-throughput data tasks. The m5ad.24xlarge is designed for multi-threaded batch operations, intermediate data processing, distributed caching, and backend databases requiring local high-speed disk arrays.
